newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin takes back presidential powers - Kremlin.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin takes back presidential powers - Kremlin.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin signed a decree on Wednesday saying he was taking back presidential powers which he had transferred to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin for the period of his heart operation, the Kremlin said.
The powers he had transferred to Chernomyrdin included the nuclear button, the ultimate control over Russia's vast nuclear arsenal.

Yeltsin's press secretary, Sergei Yastrzhembsky, said by telephone from his Kremlin office that Yeltsin signed the decree at 6 a.m. (0300 GMT), or 23 hours after he had delegated his powers to Chernomyrdin and went under the surgeon's knife.
Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin felt better than his doctors had expected. "He surprises doctors with his good state. He feels quite well for this stage," he said.
Doctors said earlier that Yeltsin's seven-hour operation included five bypasses.
